steps.prompt: What is the remainder when $47 \times 58$ is divided by $9$? Can you find it without multiplying the big numbers?

cards.title: Work with remainders only
cards.body: When you add, subtract or multiply, you can replace each number by its remainder first, then take the remainder at the end. We write $a \equiv b \pmod{m}$ ("$a$ is congruent to $b$ mod $m$") when $a$ and $b$ leave the same remainder after dividing by $m$: $47 \equiv 2 \pmod{9}$.

cards.title: Worked example: a product
cards.problem: What is the remainder when $47 \times 58$ is divided by $9$?

try.prompt: What is the remainder when $58$ is divided by $9$?
What is the remainder when $47 \times 58$ is divided by $9$?

cards.title: Powers and negative remainders
cards.body: Powers work too: if $b \equiv 1$, then $b^n \equiv 1$. It often helps to use $-1$: $8 \equiv -1 \pmod{9}$, so $8^{n}$ is $1$ for even $n$ and $-1 \equiv 8$ for odd $n$. Days of the week are arithmetic mod $7$.

cards.title: Worked example: a known remainder
cards.problem: $n$ leaves remainder $3$ when divided by $7$. What remainder does $5n$ leave?

try.prompt: What remainder does $5n$ leave when divided by $7$?

cards.title: The common trap: forgetting to reduce
cards.body: A remainder must be smaller than the divisor: $15$ is not a remainder when dividing by $7$. You can't divide inside a remainder calculation the way you multiply. And "remainder $2$ when divided by $3$ and by $5$" means $2$ more than a multiple of $\text{lcm}(3, 5) = 15$.

prompts: Where else have you seen arithmetic that "wraps around", like a clock?
